howDoI.q: How do I make light and shade with blocks?
How do I make light fade away from a lamp?
Can a lamp follow my hero?

How do I light a whole room at once?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Lights Out is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. This one is about light. Game-Maker has none: a game is blocks and a palette. So light is only paint, blocks drawn brighter than the blocks beside them. It has three short levels in a friendly dark cave. Each takes a minute or two.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

The Left and Right arrows walk and Space jumps. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

Nothing in this game can hurt you. For one map with two looks, see Day and Night and The Same House; for a block that changes when touched, see Looks Like a Wall; for blocks that change by themselves, see Flicker and Flow.

pages.head: Level 1: The Lantern Cave
pages.html:
Level 1: The Lantern Cave

A cave with three lamps on posts. FIVE SHADES OF ONE BLOCK stands near the start, RINGS GET DARKER AWAY FROM A LAMP after the first lamp, and THE LAMP STAYS PUT. KIT WALKS ON. after the second. Walk along the floor and watch it brighten and dim.

There is nothing to collect. The floor's edge, the signs and Kit are always bright enough to see.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • One block, five brightnesses. Open lanterns.bbl in the blocks editor. Every kind of block in the cave is drawn in up to five brightnesses, darkest to brightest: air.0 to air.4, rock.0.0 and up (the last number is a second layout, so a wall does not look like wallpaper), floor.0.0 and up, drip.0 and up for the stalactites and post.0 and up. A brightness is only drawn where a ring reaches it: no floor is as near a lamp as the air beside it. They are plain blocks with no rules except that rock and floor are solid. The number is the brightness, 0 for the dark and 4 right beside a lamp.
  • The light is laid in rings. Nothing glows. In the map editor the cells within a block and a half of a lantern are the brightness 4 blocks, within two and a half blocks they are 3, within three and a half 2, within four and three quarters 1, and everything farther is 0. So the floor beside a lamp is floor.3.0, a stalactite above it drip.1 and the air between air.4. The rings follow the ground: the little hill by the second lamp is lit where it rises.
  • A ramp of colors for each, in the palette. Open cave.pal in the palette editor. After the Starters' colors it has three ramps of its own: cair (6 colors), crock (8) and cfloor (8), each going from deep blue-black to a warm glow. A block of brightness k uses colors k, k+1 and k+2 of its ramp, so two neighbors of different brightness never share a color and the rings can be seen. A floor's top edge uses color k+3, brighter than the air above it, so the path can be seen even in the dark.
  • Kit and the signs keep their colors. They use the Starters' own bright colors, which stand out from every shade. The contrast of the floor's edge and of Kit against the air at each brightness is checked when the game is built.
  • The lamp. lantern is a block in the air with a flame in it, standing on post.4. It does nothing but sit there; the rings round it were laid by hand.

pages.head: Level 2: Light Your Way
pages.html:
Level 2: Light Your Way

A long dark tunnel. TOUCH A DARK BLOCK AND IT LIGHTS stands at the start, A JUMP LIGHTS BLOCKS HIGHER UP in the middle and LIGHT STAYS WHERE YOU WALKED near the door. Walk, then look back.

Jump a few times as you go.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • A dark block that lights when touched. Open tunnel.bbl and pick tdark.3. It is drawn exactly like air.0, the darkest air. On its Touch tab, Becomes block is tlit.3, a block drawn like air.3. Kit is two blocks tall and walks through the tunnel, so he touches the blocks round him and each one he touches turns lit. The dark ones he has not reached stay dark.
  • Three heights. The air close to the floor is tdark.3, which lights to tlit.3; above Kit's head it is tdark.2 and tdark.1, which light less. So a jump reaches higher blocks and lights them dimly, like light that spreads.
  • A trail, not a lantern. A touch changes only the block touched, so the light stays where Kit was. It does not come with him. The signs stand on the dark air and are not touched, so a patch behind each stays dark.

pages.head: Level 3: The Lights Come On
pages.html:
Level 3: The Lights Come On

A dark hall with three cold lamps and six bulbs over the first sign. WAIT FOR ALL SIX BULBS stands at the start and A CLOCK LIGHTS EVERY BLOCK AT ONCE after it. Wait by the door and watch: the bulbs glow one by one, and when the sixth does, the whole hall lights in one blink.

It takes about nine seconds. Then walk on to the door; the lamps and the rings are the same as in level 1.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 3 is made

  • A dark twin for every bright block. Open hall.bbl and pick floor.3.0.dark. It is drawn like floor.0.0, the dark floor. Its Next block is floor.3.0 and its Time is 168 ticks (there are 18.2 ticks in a second, so about nine seconds). Every block of the hall that is brighter than 0 is laid as a twin like this: air.2.dark turns into air.2, rock.1.1.dark into rock.1.1, and so on, and the cold lantern.dark into the lit lantern. The blocks they turn into never change again.
  • One clock lights every cell at once. The engine keeps one clock for each kind of block, not for each place on the map. When floor.3.0.dark's time is up, every cell of it in the hall becomes floor.3.0 in the same tick. Every twin has the same time, so the whole hall lights together. It is the closest a block has to a light switch: one that flips by itself.
  • Six bulbs count it down. bulb.0.off turns into bulb.0 after 28 ticks, bulb.1.off after 56, and so on to bulb.5.off after 168, the same as the hall's twins. The bulbs are the level's visible timer.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

  • Light cannot follow Kit. A block's picture never depends on where the hero stands, and the game has no lights. A lamp is paint laid in the map, so it stays where it is. Level 2 leaves a trail of light behind Kit; it does not carry a lantern with him.
  • A touch lights only the block touched. Touching one block cannot light the blocks beside it, so a switch cannot light a room. The only change that reaches many blocks at once is a block's own clock, and that clock starts when the level starts, not when Kit does something. That is why level 3 lights by itself, after a wait.
  • There are five steps, not a fade. Each brightness is a separate block with its own colors, and the rings show as steps. More steps mean more blocks, and a block set holds 150 of them: level 1 uses 79, level 2 68 and level 3, with its twins, 96. A scene can also choose another palette (see Day and Night), which changes every color at once but not the rings.
  • Monsters and the hero are not dimmed. They are drawn as they are in the light and in the dark, which is why Kit can always be seen.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • In lanterns.map, move a lamp and repaint the rings round its new place with the brighter blocks. Notice how much of the work is the rings.
  • In cave.pal, make the crock ramp's brightest colors blue and see the cave turn to moonlight.
  • In tunnel.bbl, set the Becomes block of tdark.3 to a block drawn bright green and watch Kit leave a green trail.
  • In hall.bbl, change the Time of every .dark block to a smaller number, and of the bulbs to match.
  • Draw a sixth brightness between 3 and 4 for a smoother ring.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.
